correctness.rationale: The claim gives an exact domain and strict positive rate assumptions. The proof verifies that neutral eigenvectors are exactly the Hamiltonian dark eigenvectors, so the complement decays; distinct toroidal energy values are shown to correspond exactly to signed-permutation orbits via the p-th cyclotomic polynomial and a histogram-sum constraint. Fourier-character independence reduces each spectral block to its number of distinct projected frequencies. A complete analysis of all eight group elements on each affine momentum fiber yields the axis/diagonal, generic and square-root-minus-one counts for all odd primes p≥5. Independent exact modular Krylov ranks over two moduli agree at p=5,7,11,13, and Fourier orbit enumeration agrees for all slopes at p=3,5,7,11,13,17,19,23,29. No finite test is used to prove the infinite statement.

originality.rationale: The original quantitative statement is the three-way, all-odd-prime classification of the rank of a full affine line of sinks in the nearest-neighbor quantum torus, with an exceptional slope if and only if -1 is a finite-field square. The general dark-space reduction is already known and explicitly attributed. Direct searches and inspected primary text reveal ring, single-trap torus and general-network work, not a statement implying the all-prime orientation-dependent rank formulas. Historical priority remains provisional, particularly because the 1988 Torney report was not fully read.
residual_risks: Historical priority is not independently verified, especially possible implicit implications in Torney 1988 full report, which was not read completely.
Related unpublished or not indexed work could already include the explicit prime-line slope count.
The spectral separation lemma is an elementary consequence of the prime cyclotomic polynomial; novelty is asserted for the complete placement law rather than that ingredient in isolation.

value.rationale: A single natural design constraint—p equal-count absorbers on a line of the homogeneous prime square torus—has three sharply different observable subspace sizes. Axial and diagonal choices capture about one half of a maximally mixed excitation, while generic slopes capture all but O(p) modes; an exact p≡1 mod4 congruence further halves the residual dark-mode leading constant. This is an interpretable, quantitatively large network-geometry effect and a complete placement classification in a motivated infinite family, not a routine isolated graph calculation. It does not claim finite-time efficiency or arbitrary absorber-set optimality.
